transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess… it’s mostly that I’m spending a lot more time than I should checking things. Like dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes at work—things like that. I know it probably sounds excessive, but I feel like I can’t really move on until I’ve gone through the routine enough times that I feel calmer. It’s starting to take hours, and I’m not handling it as well as I’d like.
Can you tell me if you have any recurring thoughts or worries that come up while you’re checking these things, something that feels intrusive or unwanted?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know on some level I’ve already cleaned the wound area or checked the CAD file properly, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m being careless or anything. But this thought kind of cuts in like, what if I missed one tiny thing?

Like with a wound, it’s “what if that little thing becomes an infection,” and at work it’s more like, “what if there’s one design mistake I missed and someone gets hurt because of it.” I can tell myself I reviewed it, but it doesn’t really settle just from reasoning it through, if that makes sense.
Do these checking behaviors help reduce the anxiety or discomfort that comes with those thoughts, or are you mainly trying to prevent something bad from happening?

I think… both, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing it for no reason, because in the moment it feels like I’m being responsible. But what actually happens is I keep rechecking the dressing supplies, the door locks, the file dimensions, the revision notes… and I don’t really feel allowed to move on until I’ve done the routine enough times that the anxiety comes down.

So yes, it’s to prevent something bad, I guess, but also it’s because I feel so uncomfortable if I stop too soon. Does that make sense?

Can you tell me if the anxiety you feel when you stop checking too soon is related to a specific fear of something happening, like an infection or an accident, or if it’s more of a general discomfort that something isn’t quite right?

It’s… more specific, I think. I mean, there is that general “not right” feeling, but it usually has a fear attached to it.

Like even if I know I cleaned the wound area, the thought keeps popping in that maybe I missed one small spot and it could turn into an infection. Or with a CAD file, I’ll know I reviewed it, but then I get this thought that one tiny mistake could be there and somehow someone could get hurt because of it.

I know that probably sounds a bit extreme, and I can sometimes tell myself it’s unlikely, but it doesn’t really go away just because I reason it through.

Have you ever performed checking rituals not because you were afraid something bad would happen, but simply because you felt a strong inner need for things to feel 'just right' or to reduce a feeling of discomfort without a clear feared outcome?

I think… maybe not totally without a feared outcome. Most of the time there is some worry behind it.

But there’s also this feeling that I’m not allowed to move on until I’ve done the checking routine enough times. Like with the dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes… I can lose hours rechecking them, and part of it is that I’m waiting for the anxiety to drop or for it to feel okay enough to stop.

I don’t know if that counts as “just right,” exactly. It’s not like I enjoy it or want it perfect for its own sake. It’s more like I feel stuck until it feels safe enough or settled enough. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if there are times when you have distressing thoughts or images that you can’t seem to get out of your mind, even if you don’t act on them with checking or rituals?

Yes… I think that does happen. I don’t always act on it right away, or at least I try not to, but the thought can still keep coming back.

Like even after I know I cleaned the wound area, my mind cuts in with, “What if you missed one tiny spot and it turns into an infection?” Or after I’ve reviewed a CAD file, I’ll get this image or thought that there’s one small mistake in there and someone could get hurt because of it.

I can tell myself, logically, that I already checked it and that it’s probably fine, but it doesn’t really… settle. It keeps pushing back in. I don’t know if I’m explaining that correctly.

Can you tell me if you feel driven to perform these checking routines very specifically, like a certain number of times or in a particular way, in order to feel less anxious or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always like a magic number exactly, but I do feel like I have to do it in the same way, or enough times, before I’m allowed to stop.

Like with my dressing supplies, the door locks, file dimensions, revision notes… I’ll recheck them, and then I’ll doubt whether I really checked properly, so I go through it again. And I can lose hours that way, which is embarrassing to admit.

I guess the goal is for the anxiety to drop enough that I can move on, or to feel like I’ve prevented something bad from slipping through. I know that probably sounds irrational, but in the moment it feels hard to just stop.
Can you tell me if there are times when you have these distressing thoughts or images but you deliberately resist doing any checking or mental rituals, even though it’s hard?

Yes… sometimes I do try to resist it. I don’t always succeed, but I’ll try to just sit with it and not go back and check again.

Like, even when I know I cleaned the wound area, the thought still cuts in that maybe I missed one tiny thing and it could turn into an infection. Or with a CAD file, after I’ve already reviewed it, I’ll get this thought that there’s one small mistake in there and someone could get hurt.

I try to tell myself, “No, you already did it,” and not do the checking again, but it’s hard because I can’t really reason it away. It just keeps pressing on me. I don’t know if that’s the kind of resistance you mean.
Can you tell me if you ever perform checking behaviors mainly to reduce the anxiety or discomfort you feel, even if you don’t necessarily believe something bad will happen if you stop?

Yeah… I think that’s probably a big part of it, honestly. It’s not always that I’m completely convinced something terrible will happen if I stop right then. Sometimes it’s more that I just feel… unsettled, like I’m not allowed to move on yet.

So I’ll recheck things like my dressing supplies, or the door locks, or file dimensions and revision notes at work, and I know it may be more than I need to. But if I don’t go through the routine enough times, the anxiety just stays there. I end up losing hours to it sometimes, which I know isn’t ideal.

I guess I’m doing it to get that feeling to drop enough that I can continue. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if you ever perform these checking behaviors mainly to quiet the uncomfortable feeling or anxiety itself, even if you don’t think something specific will actually go wrong?

Yes… I think that is probably true. It’s a little embarrassing to put it that way, but a lot of the checking is less about one clear disaster I’m picturing and more about trying to quiet that feeling that something is unfinished or not safe enough.

I’ll go back over my dressing supplies, the door locks, file dimensions, revision notes… things like that. And I don’t feel like I’m allowed to move on until I’ve done it the same way, or enough times, that the anxiety comes down.

I know that might sound excessive, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I can lose hours to it. That’s really what brought me in.
